body:
- Implementation of model descriptor part by new `Descriptor` interface. 
- fix bugs of the dpa1 and dpa2 implementations 
- fix some direct access of class "private" variables. 
- fix jit compiling issue of neighbor list. It seems that jit only support `Dict[str, xxx]`, where the key must be `str`. 
- remove the initialization of a type embedding in `repformers`
- point out BAD designs, that are using model dict for passing information to dataloader and trainer. Clear interface should be given in future PRs. 
- we do not support list of nlists, because multiple nlist can be easily made from a nlist that has the maximal cut-off radius and nsel. 
- type embedding treated as descriptor. the dpa1 and dpa2 descriptors concatenate the type embedding before output. the fitting net will not take type embedding in the future. 
- switch off the support of hybrid. hybrid with concat will be added back in the future PRs. 
- fix the smoothness issue of dpa1 when dotr is applied. now the behavior should be same as https://github.com/deepmodeling/deepmd-kit/blob/839f4fe74ad321c679f709e337a8e95b15fa5c63/deepmd/descriptor/se_atten.py#L876-L891

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a

author: macil
body:
I've been working on my own vkQuake fork that may or may not end up going anywhere, and had been considering porting bugfixes from QS+QSS+Ironwail, and I'm excited to find this fork that's done some of that work already. Though I noticed a few things that could be improved in your repo, and figured it would be good to do that for your benefit and to make it easier to share work in the future.

I recommend viewing this PR commit by commit, as the final commit contains the results of running clang-format on the codebase and has a lot of random whitespace changes. I considered separating this into multiple PRs, but they're dependent on each other and work together to get CI fully working, so I figured it was simplest to do it this way.

The first commit fixes the Meson build config being broken from when you updated Mimalloc. The Meson build config is optional on Windows but it's used by the Github Actions CI workflows and I think it's necessary to compile on MacOS and/or Linux because it's what I've been using there.

The second commit changes the Github Action CI workflows to run on commits on all branches. Original vkQuake had the Linux, Mac, and non-mingw Windows CI workflows set to only run on the master branch, which is unnecessarily stingy when actions are fully free to use on public repos and probably caused you to never see that they were failing to build because you only worked in a non-master branch.

The third commit updates the Github Action CI workflows to use the latest versions of various things, fixing it using some unsupported systems (macos-11 and ubuntu 18.04) and some of these updates include some performance improvements for CI. Additionally I prettied up vkQuake's atrociously formatted run-in-docker.sh script. The only real changes in this commit are in the .clang-format files and in the .github/workflows/clang-format-check.yml file.

The fourth commit gets the Formatting Check workflow passing again, and makes it work with the current version of clang-format instead of requiring code to be formatted with an old version. Original vkQuake had all of its code kept in format with clang-format v15, and a couple small spots of it were impacted by the move to v17. (Most of the files impacted are from your changes.) Code formatters are pretty nice imo and the cost of breaking consistency with past forks was already mostly paid when vkQuake reformatted all of its code inherited from Quakespasm, so I think it's worth continuing the practice like this, though you could always leave this commit out.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or
  omit wouldn't work correctly (`issue 1604`_).  This is now fixed, with
  testing help by `Marc Gibbons <pull 1608_>`_.

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using
  relative files and the source option ended with a slash (`issue 1541`_).
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Kevin Brown-Silva <pull 1608_>`_.

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a
  terminal-compatible URL, so that you can click the location to open the HTML
  file in

body:
The Raised mod has changed where it looks for the file `hotbar_selection.png`. It now provides its own internal copy at `assets/raised/textures/gui/sprites/hud/hotbar_selection.png`, and also will only apply replacement textures if they are specified at that location.

The recent changes to GUI structuring within the newest resource pack formats have cut off `hotbar_selection.png` so that it is no longer a square, and VanillaXBR does already correctly reflect this. This PR would restore compatibility with Raised by adding an additional version that **_IS_** a square, in the location that Raised is looking.

I have tested this change on my computer with the latest release of Raised, and I can confirm it works.

author: james-garriss
body:
## 🗣 Description ##

After adding the MegaLinter (ML) PowerShell linter, we had two linters for PowerShell, both of which used PS Script Analyzer (PSA).  The original workflow was not working; that is, it never returned any linting issues.  The newer one that used ML was working fine.  The original was based upon code created by an [individual](https://github.com/devblackops) and has not been updated for a couple years.  I tested with both the [GitHub Action and Docker versions](https://github.com/devblackops/github-action-psscriptanalyzer), but neither worked.  In the end, I removed the old workflow and kept the new one.   Using ML allows us to add as many different linters as we want using the same tool and nearly the same workflows.

## 💭 Motivation and context ##

There is no reason to have two workflows that use the same linter for PS.

## 🧪 Testing ##

I tested by pushing code and viewing the results in Actions.

- [x] This PR has an informative and human-readable title.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.3** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or
  omit wouldn't work correctly (`issue 1604`_).  This is now fixed, with
  testing help by `Marc Gibbons <pull 1608_>`_.

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using
  relative files and the source option ended with a slash (`issue 1541`_).
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Kevin Brown-Silva <pull 1608_>`_.

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a
  terminal-compatible URL, so that you can click the location to open the HTML
  file

This addresses #108.

## Type of change

Run the following snippet twice:

```python
!pip install roboflow

from roboflow import Roboflow
rf = Roboflow(api_key="")

body: The pinmapping for the Launchpad and the actual PCB (Nsumo) are represented with an enum (io_e). The result is an abstraction that's much nicer than directly accessing the crude register variables from TI.

author: eve-ning
body:
# Major Changes

This PR is mainly to clean up some code smell in the repository. Specifically targetting the code that's used in the `model_test` for Chestnut May Dec.

- Implement `FRDCDatasetPreset`, an interface to specify pre-defined datasets without having to remember the exact paths for it in GCS
- Implement **unlabelled dataset** fetching from `FRDCDatasetPreset`.
- Implement `__add__` op for `FRDCDataset` as an alias to create the concatenated `FRDCConcatDataset`
- Migrate `train.py` common utilities to `frdc/utils/training.py`

>[!WARNING]
> - Removed expose for `frdc.load`, all imports for `FRDCDataset` now must be fully specified `import frdc.load.dataset import FRDCDataset`
> 
> ```python
> # Previously
> from frdc.load import FRDCDataset
> 
> # Now
> from frdc.load.dataset import FRDCDataset
> ```
> We did this to avoid future headaches on circular imports as **presets** depend on `frdc.load`

## Minor Changes

- Clean up `on_before_batch_transfer` for `MixMatchModule`, the preprocessing step.
- Split `evaluate` function in `train.py` to more granular steps: `predict`, `plot_confusion_matrix`, `accuracy`
- `FRDCDataModule` will accept labelled datasets, which will be casted to an unlabelled dataset internally.
- `_load_debug_dataset` is deprecated in favour of using `FRDCDatasetPreset`'s `DEBUG`

## `FRDCDatasetPreset`

Currently, getting the dataset is flaky, as we need to memorize the exact dataset path. 
To solve this, we hardcode some common datasets in GCS into variables.
These hardcoded values can be accessed via `FRDCDatasetPreset`

```python
from frdc.load.dataset import FRDCDataset
from frdc.load.preset import FRDCDatasetPreset

# Previously
train_lab_ds = FRDCDataset(
    "chestnut_nature_park",
    "20201218",
    None,
    transform=train_preprocess,
)

# Now
train_lab_ds = ds.chestnut_20201218(transform=train_preprocess)
```

As shown, the syntax is simpler, the new way simply **curries** the original constructor, exposing only the additional arguments, `transform,target_transform,...`

>[!NOTE]
> Currying (also known as partial functions) helps fill in part of the function without actually evaluating it.
> For example, we can curry an `add(a, b)` function to `add_2(a)` by currying `b=2`.
> In this case, the developer only has to specify `a`, never `b`.

>[!TIP]
>`FRDCDataset` still functions as is, so if there's a new dataset, not yet defined by the hardcoded values, it's still possible to initialize from there.

### Unlabelled Dataset

Some of our architectures depend on the `DataLoader` returning only the **unlabelled** data, so with `FRDCDatasetPreset`, you can get the `unlabelled` variant.

```python
from frdc.load.dataset import FRDCDataset
from frdc.load.preset import FRDCDatasetPreset

# Previously
train_unl_ds = FRDCUnlabelledDataset(
    "chestnut_nature_park",
    "20201218",
    None,
    transform=train_unl_preprocess(2),

# Now
train_unl_ds = ds.chestnut_20201218.unlabelled(
    transform=train_unl_preprocess(2)
)
```

Similarly to the above, we yield the unlabelled variant by a method.

>[!TIP]
> To keep the syntax consistent, you can consider `ds.chestnut_20201218.labelled(...)` which is an alias to `ds.chestnut_20201218()`.

## `__add__` op for Dataset Concatenation

Currently, we planned for `FRDCConcatDataset([ds1, ds2, ...])` which can be a bit cumbersome to type.
We now override the `__add__` op on `FRDCDataset`, so now you can simply use `ds1 + ds2` to concatenate datasets.

Given that `ds1` and `ds2` are `FRDCDataset`s.

```python
ds = ds1 + ds2
```

`ds` will be ` FRDCConcatDataset`.

Furthermore, you can add more datasets to the concat dataset

```python
ds = ds1 + ds2
ds = ds + ds3
```

>[!WARNING]
>We have not tested the performance of this yet, we suspect it may be slow if you concat many datasets via this method. This is because every addition calls the `__init__` of `FRDCConcatDataset`.
>We recommend to do `FRDCConcatDataset([ds1, ds2, ...])` if it gets too slow.

# What does this implement/fix?

This adds the method `queue_size()` to Nextion component.
This function returns the current count of commands that have been queued but not yet processed for the Nextion display. The Nextion command queue is used to store commands that are sent to the Nextion display for various operations like updating the display, changing interface elements, or other interactive features. A larger queue size might indicate a higher processing time or potential delays in command execution. This function is useful for monitoring the command flow and managing the execution efficiency of the Nextion display interface.

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.0** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or
  omit wouldn't work correctly (`issue 1604`_).  This is now fixed, with
  testing help by `Marc Gibbons <pull 1608_>`_.

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using
  relative files and the source option ended with a slash (`issue 1541`_).
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Kevin Brown-Silva <pull 1608_>`_.

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a
  terminal-compatible URL, so that you can click the location to open the HTML
  file in

author: sbuerk
body:
PHPUnit changed the error handler behaviour and introduced the PHP
attribute `#[WithoutErrorHandler]` to omit the error handler for
test methods.

This breaks the dangling error handler check provided by the
`typo3/testing-framework` which assumes that the PHPUnit error
handler is always the only registered error handler.

This change modifies the `BaseTestCase` class

* to provide the borrowed `shouldErrorHandlerBeUsed()` method
  cloned from `TestRunner` with additional version guards.
* to align the dangling error handler check in the `tearDown()`
  method of the `BaseTestCase` class using the added method.

Releases: main, 7
Related: https://forge.typo3.org/issues/102724

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or
  omit wouldn't work correctly (`issue 1604`_).  This is now fixed, with
  testing help by `Marc Gibbons <pull 1608_>`_.

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using
  relative files and the source option ended with a slash (`issue 1541`_).
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Kevin Brown-Silva <pull 1608_>`_.

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a
  terminal-compatible URL, so that you can click the location to open the HTML
  file in

author: nischalkothari
body:
In the refined code, several optimizations have been introduced to enhance the efficiency of the bubble sort algorithm. Notably, a check has been incorporated to determine whether the input array is already sorted. If the array is sorted, the new implementation intelligently avoids unnecessary iterations beyond the first pass of the bubble sort algorithm.

Key Points:

Array Sorting Optimization:
1. The code now features an improved sorting algorithm that intelligently detects whether the array is already sorted.
2. If the array is confirmed to be sorted, the algorithm skips additional iterations beyond the first pass of the bubble sort.

Reduced Iterations for Sorted Arrays:
1. Unlike the previous version, the updated code ensures a significant reduction in iterations when dealing with already sorted arrays.
2. This optimization translates to enhanced time complexity, especially in scenarios where the array is in a pre-sorted state.

These enhancements contribute to a more efficient and time-saving implementation of the bubble sort algorithm, particularly when sorting arrays with varying degrees of order.

body:
### Pull Request Description

I noticed that sources in `runtime/bench` are not formatted at all. Turns out that the `JavaFormatterPlugin` does not override `javafmt` task for the `Benchmark` configuration. After some failed attempts, I have just redefined the `Benchmark/javafmt` task in the `runtime` project. After all, the `runtime` project is almost the only project where we have any Java benchmarks.

### Important Notes

`javafmtAll` now also formats sources in `runtime/bench/src/java`.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.0.3** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or
  omit wouldn't work correctly (`issue 1604`_).  This is now fixed, with
  testing help by `Marc Gibbons <pull 1608_>`_.

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using
  relative files and the source option ended with a slash (`issue 1541`_).
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Kevin Brown-Silva <pull 1608_>`_.

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a
  terminal-compatible URL, so that you can click the location to open the HTML
  file

author: klemendev
body:
In some cases, OGG sounds play in MCreator but not in Minecraft, in some cases, sounds don't play in MCreator but do in Minecraft.

This is because different audio libraries are used by both software.

As this confuses users in quite some scenarios, we are better off not having a play button at the time of writing.

An alternative is to ship the whole LWJGL (lwjgl openal library is used by Minecraft) with MCreator which is currently an overkill.

<details>

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209

   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646

## Which issue does this PR close?

Currently, the serializer is re-created for each RecordBatch, which degrades the performance while dealing with small batch sizes.

Also, this makes the internal buffer useless since it is re-created for each batch in this setup.

- Renamed the `BatchSerializer`.

author: amish1188
body:
Nå skal dist mappe inneholde kun bundlet prosjekt (komponenter), css fil med alle token varianter og global.css fil, og src mappe med kun komponenter. 

For å bygge bibliotek på en riktig måte må vi inkludere dist mappe (med bundled prosjekt) i publisering. Ellers skal pakken ikke fungere på en riktig måte (bl.a. node modules skal ikke med som f.eks. gjør at ts dekoratorer ikke fungerer som de burde).  Per i dag skjer det ikke fordi vi ignorerer dist mappe i .gitignore mappe. Hvis biblioteket ikke inneholder .npmignore fil, .gitignore er tatt som default (derfor dist blir ignorert). 
Jeg oppdaterte viteconfig fil så at den bundler kun src/index.ts fil (altså alle komponenter som vi eksporterer) og at bundlet fil alltid heter nve-designsystem. Vi oppretter også umd bundled fil som støtter eldre nettlesere der hvor esmodules ikke støttes, men også andre miljøer som node.js. global.css blir en del av js kode nå så at vi slipper å importere global.css når vi skal bruke komponentene.
 
Det var en del problemer med å lage type fil (.d.ts) under bygging som burde bli opprettet som default, derfor installerte jeg vite-plugin-dts for å sikre at den kjøres. Vi trenger types ( "declaration": true, "emitDeclarationOnly": true, i tsconfig sikrer at de opprettes) for å vise dem på en riktig måte når man importerer komponenter i andre prosjekter. 

Jeg lagde en script build.js fordi det var ganske mange filkopiering og npm script i package.json startet å se litt stygt ut. Kan være at build.js skal utvides senere enda mer, så det er kanskje lurt å ha alt i en separat .js fil istedenfor. La til publish script også men for nå kjører den kun npm pack (for lokal testing). Vi må gjerne endre den til å kjøre npm publish når den blir integrert til pipelinen. 

Jeg endret fil struktur som vi snakket om, altså alle komponenter har nå .components.ts suffix osv.

Jeg la til reflect:true på alle properties i komponentene fordi hvis man ikke har de, vises de ikke i DOMen i reactive rammeverker som Vue (da overskriver vue shadow domen med sin egen css bundling og man ser ikke properties, og derfor styling fungerer ikke heller).

Jeg oppdaterte dokumentasjon nå. Viktig steg er å teste pakke lokalt ved å installere zippet pakke som reflekterer hvordan alt skal fungere akkurat som man hadde installert det. Det er bedre måte å teste med npm pack enn med npm link. 

La også tgz filer til .gitignore i tilfelle folk glemmer å slette test pakker før de pusher til repo :P

author: jart
body:
The default values for tfs_z and typical_p were being set to zero, which caused the token candidates array to get shrunk down to one element thus preventing any sampling. Note this only applies to OpenAI API compatible HTTP server requests.

The solution is to use the default values that OpenAI documents, as well as ensuring we use the llama.cpp defaults for the rest. I've tested this change still ensures deterministic output by default. If a "temperature" greater than 0 is explicitly passed, then output is unique each time. If "seed" is specified in addition to "temperature" then the output becomes deterministic once more.

See mozilla-Ocho/llamafile#117
See mozilla-Ocho/llamafile@9e4bf29

author: hop311
body:
This will be followed by a main repo PR implementing the corresponding changes there.

- Renamed `GameAdvancementHook` to `SimulationClock` and added a callback for clock state change (pause or speed changes) to be used to update the UI indepdently of full gamestate updates. Also added pause control functions, replacing the previous direct use of a public `is_paused` variable.
- Renamed `update_state` / `state_updated` functions to `update_gamestate` / `gamestate_updated` to avoid confusion with clock state and actual in game `State`s.
- Added `currently_updating_gamestate` flag to detect recursive/chain updates (updating the gamestate shouldn't queue another update).
- Fixed issue with `Climate` loading where they were being locked before cross-climate duplicates were removed.
- Fixed `vec2_t` component type cast being non-const.
- Removed `.git` extension from lexy-vdf submodule URL to be consistent with the repo's other submodules.
- Swapped `GFX::ProgressBar`'s `progress_colour` and `back_colour` in its parsing function, so that `color` is front/progress and `colortwo` is back/base, matching how they're used in the defines.

author: jepler
body:
I noticed that when placing legends on cherry keycaps, the depth varies across the key. This is because the text is placed on a plane, not along the curve of the top key surface.

I'm printing resin keycaps then adding color legends using gel nail polish; I think that having consistent depth of the inset legends will lead to better results.

I investigated options to correct this. One possibility is the openscad "text on" library. Of course, this library comes with its own set of caveats, many resulting from the fact that it's not possible to directly measure text metrics from within scad code.

Here's the result of my experimentation. I don't think it's suitable to merge in its current state, so please consider this a possible starting point for discussion.

This copies in the text_on library, which I believe is licensed compatibly (LGPL 2.1 upgrades to GPL2-or-later, which in turn upgrades to GPL3).

Please feel free to close this up if it's not a direction you're interested in pursuing. In any case, thanks for KeyV2.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **6.3.2** to **7.4.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- In Python 3.12 and above, you can try an experimental core based on the new
  :mod:`sys.monitoring <python:sys.monitoring>` module by defining a
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` environment variable.  This should be faster, though
  plugins and dynamic contexts are not yet supported with it.  I am very
  interested to hear how it works (or doesn't!) for you.


.. _changes_7-3-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the change for multi-line signature exclusions in 7.3.3 broke other
  forms of nested clauses being excluded properly.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 1713`_.

- Fix: in the HTML report, selecting code for copying won't select the line
  numbers also. Thanks, `Robert Harris <pull 1717_>`_.

.. _issue 1713: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1713
.. _pull 1717: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1717


.. _changes_7-3-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209
.. _pull 1650: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1650

.. _changes_7-3-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

- Docs: examples of configuration files now include separate examples for the
  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

- Added a CITATION.cff file, thanks to `Ken Schackart <pull 1641_>`_.

.. _pull 1641: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1641
.. _issue 1646: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1646


.. _changes_7-2-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: reverted a `change from 6.4.3 <pull 1347b_>`_ that helped Cython, but
  also increased the size of data files when using dynamic contexts, as
  described in the now-fixed `issue 1586`_. The problem is now avoided due to a
  recent change (`issue 1538 <issue 1538b_>`_).  Thanks to `Anders Kaseorg
  <pull 1629_>`_ and David Szotten for persisting with problem reports and
  detailed diagnoses.

- Wheels are now provided for CPython 3.12.

.. _pull 1347b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1347
.. _issue 1538b: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1538
.. _issue 1586: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1586
.. _pull 1629: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1629


.. _changes_7-2-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the ``lcov`` command could raise an IndexError exception if a file is
  translated to Python but then executed under its own name.  Jinja2 does this
  when rendering templates.  Fixes `issue 1553`_.

- Python 3.12 beta 1 now inlines comprehensions.  Previously they were compiled
  as invisible functions and coverage.py would warn you if they weren't
  completely executed.  This no longer happens under Python 3.12.

- Fix: the ``coverage debug sys`` command includes some environment variables
  in its output.  This could have included sensitive data.  Those values are
  now hidden with asterisks, closing `issue 1628`_.

.. _issue 1553: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1553
.. _issue 1628: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1628


.. _changes_7-2-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ``html_report()`` could fail with an AttributeError on ``isatty`` if run
  in an unusual environment where sys.stdout had been replaced.  This is now
  fixed.


.. _changes_7-2-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.4
   ```
   --------------------------

PyCon 2023 sprint fixes!

- Fix: with ``relative_files = true``, specifying a specific file to include or
  omit wouldn't work correctly (`issue 1604`_).  This is now fixed, with
  testing help by `Marc Gibbons <pull 1608_>`_.

- Fix: the XML report would have an incorrect ``<source>`` element when using
  relative files and the source option ended with a slash (`issue 1541`_).
  This is now fixed, thanks to `Kevin Brown-Silva <pull 1608_>`_.

- When the HTML report location is printed to the terminal, it's now a
  terminal-compatible URL, so that you can click the location to open the HTML
  file
